title: Sheshbazzar
lead: Sheshbazzar, called "the leader of Judah" and "governor," received the Temple vessels from Cyrus and led the first return from Babylon in 538 BC (Ezra 1:8–11; Ezra 5:14–16). Whether he was the same man as Zerubbabel has been debated since ancient times.

sections.b: Ezra credits Sheshbazzar with laying the Temple's foundation (Ezra 5:16), but also tells how Zerubbabel and Jeshua laid it (Ezra 3:8–10), and Zechariah says "Zerubbabel's hands founded this house" (Zechariah 4:9, translated fresh). Some readers have therefore taken the two names as one man, as Daniel and his friends bore Babylonian names. Most modern scholars, following Sara Japhet and others, think they were two leaders: Sheshbazzar, the official appointed by Cyrus, and Zerubbabel, of David's line, who led the work under Darius. 1 Esdras names both together (1 Esdras 6:18). A popular identification with Shenazzar, a son of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:18), is possible but unproven.
